presets.title: Fix a fleet of CLIs
presets.blurb: Capacity replay: every agent runs the same scripted patch. A pass means the script finished and the hidden tests matched. It does not say who can fix a CLI.

presets.title: Nightly reports
presets.blurb: Capacity replay: one scripted report per agent, checked against the expected file. A pass is conformance to that script.

presets.title: Triage error logs
presets.blurb: Capacity replay: the script reads one log and writes the known counts. A pass is not a model triaging the log.

presets.title: Migrate configs
presets.blurb: Capacity replay: the script rewrites the configs to the known format. A pass is conformance, not a migration the harness invented.

presets.title: All of it at once
presets.blurb: Capacity replay of the four scripted jobs in one wave. The mix is the backlog shape. The solutions are already in the scripts.

presets.title: Maze: a swarm on a branchy maze (shared map)
presets.blurb: Every agent explores one hidden maze through ./maze and shares what it has mapped, so agents split the branches. The scripted explorer follows a fixed rule: a pass means that agent made only legal moves and the swarm reached the exit. Time to exit, calls and repeated work are read from the maze service's own log.

presets.title: Maze: the same swarm, no shared map
presets.blurb: The same maze and the same agents, but each one explores alone and must reach the exit itself. The comparison with the shared-map preset is what coordination buys. A pass means that agent reached the exit with legal moves.

presets.title: Maze: long corridors (negative control)
presets.blurb: A maze of long winding corridors with few branches, so there is little to split. A swarm should gain little here; if it does not, the method is wrong. Shared map, scripted explorer.

presets.title: Maze: a larger branchy maze
presets.blurb: A 64 by 40 branchy maze with a shared map, for how the gain scales. Scripted explorer; a pass means legal moves and the swarm reached the exit.

presets.title: Maze: shared map on an equal call budget
presets.blurb: The branchy maze with a total call budget equal to one agent's calls alone, so the swarm has no extra calls to spend. It shows whether coordination wins when the cost is equal.

presets.title: Cold start
presets.blurb: One model request, no tools. The number is launch to first request, and final reply to exit. Size 1 runs five rounds. Successes per minute stay blank unless the wave actually filled.

presets.title: Subagent swarm
presets.blurb: Three requests and two small writes, no shell: an operating-system process with that shape, not an in-process subagent. The collapsed protocol does both writes in one program.

presets.title: 50 tool calls
presets.blurb: Fifty shell steps, one echo at a time. The number is the step gap. The collapsed protocol writes the same ticks.txt in one program.

presets.title: 250-step session
presets.blurb: 250 shell steps. The number is context growth and the early-versus-late step gap. The collapsed protocol writes the same file in one program.

presets.title: Read 20 logs
presets.blurb: Naive protocol: one read per log, then the script writes the known answer. The number is how request bytes grow. Collapsed: one program counts the ERROR lines.

presets.title: Read 60 logs
presets.blurb: The same read-per-file protocol at 60 logs. Context slope is the number. Collapsed counts in one program. A pass does not mean the harness chose to read every file.

presets.title: Lane baseline
presets.blurb: Five size-1 startups of the mini agent on this VM. Printed beside a harness number so machine noise is visible. Not ranked.

presets.title: Lane control
presets.blurb: The mini agent on 50 shell steps, size 1, three rounds, run on this VM with every run. Each lane's time numbers are read against it. Not ranked.
